observation_summary: The PeriodFormatter fails to parse certain period strings when constructed using a specific builder pattern that mimics ISOPeriodFormat.standard(). The failure manifests as an IllegalArgumentException indicating a malformed string.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding a conditional check to the logic that assembles the PeriodFormatter from element pairs. Specifically, it ensures that the 'Separator' element is only finished (and thus the formatter chain is correctly linked) if the separator's after-parser and after-printer are null. This is a correction to the internal logic/algorithm used to build the formatter, ensuring that the composite structure is correctly initialized based on the provided elements. It is not a simple missing check (Checking) because it modifies the construction algorithm of the formatter itself, and it is not a structural change (Function/Class/Object) as it does not change the interface or add new capabilities.
evidence_used: The fix modifies the logic in PeriodFormatterBuilder.java within the method that assembles the formatter from element pairs.
The diff adds a conditional check 'if (sep.iAfterParser == null && sep.iAfterPrinter == null)' before finishing the separator.
The bug report highlights a discrepancy between a manually built formatter and the standard ISO formatter, which the fix addresses by correcting the assembly logic.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds an 'if' statement, the primary purpose is to control the algorithm for assembling the formatter components, not just to validate input data.
The fix does not involve inheritance or structural associations between classes, but rather the internal logic of how a composite object is built.
